# Azure Native MongoDB ANM — facts

> Source-anchored units about Azure Native MongoDB ANM: 18 across 3 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

## How it works

- [statement] MongoDB's native-integration documentation limits organizations created through this flow to clusters hosted on Azure. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/partner-integrations/azure.md · keywords: Azure Native MongoDB ANM
- [statement] Provisioning requires the Owner or Contributor role on the Azure subscription. The Azure creation flow collects the subscription, resource group, resource name and Atlas organization name. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-01-27) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/partner-integrations/azure.md · keywords: Azure Native MongoDB ANM · also: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/partner-solutions/mongo-db/create
- [statement] The documented onboarding flow uses a Go to MongoDB Atlas link. New users can be prompted to set an Atlas password; Azure-native provisioning alone should not be assumed to remove Atlas account setup. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-05-26) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/partner-integrations/azure.md · keywords: Azure Native MongoDB ANM · also: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/partner-solutions/mongo-db/faq
- [statement] If an organization has paid clusters when Azure billing is removed, MongoDB requires a payment method in Atlas to avoid service suspension or termination. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/partner-integrations/azure.md · keywords: Azure Native MongoDB ANM

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Microsoft and MongoDB describe the service as MongoDB Atlas as an Azure Native Integration; MongoDB abbreviates Azure Native Integration as ANI. The reviewed primary sources do not name a separate product 'Azure Native MongoDB ANM'. (high confidence) — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/partner-solutions/mongo-db/overview · keywords: Azure Native MongoDB ANM · also: https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/mongodb-atlas-now-available-as-azure-native-integration
- [statement] The integration provisions a new Atlas organization from an Azure resource and automatically connects organization billing to Azure Marketplace, with charges on the Azure invoice. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/partner-integrations/azure.md · keywords: Azure Native MongoDB ANM · also: https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/mongodb-atlas-now-available-as-azure-native-integration
- [statement] Setup requires an active Azure subscription and its Owner or Contributor role; merely discovering the marketplace offering does not grant provisioning rights. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-01-27) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/partner-integrations/azure.md · keywords: Azure Native MongoDB ANM · also: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/partner-solutions/mongo-db/create
- [statement] Provisioning grants the initiating user Atlas Organization Owner access. Atlas uses that user's Azure email address; new Atlas users must configure their Atlas account, and an already federated email domain can avoid a new password. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/partner-integrations/azure.md · keywords: Azure Native MongoDB ANM
- [statement] Azure exposes a Go to MongoDB Atlas link to access the Atlas organization. The documentation therefore describes an Azure onboarding entry point alongside a distinct Atlas portal and account setup. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-05-26) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/partner-integrations/azure.md · keywords: Azure Native MongoDB ANM · also: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/partner-solutions/mongo-db/faq
- [statement] Deleting the Azure MongoDB Atlas resource does not delete the Atlas organization. MongoDB says unlinking also removes Marketplace billing; paid clusters require a replacement payment method in Atlas to avoid service suspension or termination. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-05-26) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/partner-integrations/azure.md · keywords: Azure Native MongoDB ANM · also: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/partner-solutions/mongo-db/faq
- [statement] MongoDB's launch article records a May 14, 2025 public preview and a July 31, 2025 update announcing general availability. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/mongodb-atlas-now-available-as-azure-native-integration · keywords: Azure Native MongoDB ANM
- [statement] MongoDB's launch article lists the Azure Portal UI and CLI/SDK/ARM for creating and managing Atlas organizations. It then describes follow-on configuration and service connections from the new organization, including network and security settings using existing Azure Virtual Networks and Azure Private Link, and connections to Azure AI Foundry, Azure Databricks, or Microsoft Fabric. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/mongodb-atlas-now-available-as-azure-native-integration · keywords: Azure Native MongoDB ANM
- [statement] The official product name is MongoDB Atlas as an Azure Native Integration (ANI): Microsoft and MongoDB jointly provide an Azure entry point for provisioning Atlas organizations, with Atlas documentation describing automatic billing through the Azure invoice. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/partner-integrations/azure.md · keywords: Azure Native MongoDB ANM · also: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/partner-solutions/mongo-db/overview
- [statement] MongoDB announced general availability of Atlas as a Microsoft Azure Native Integration on July 31, 2025. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/products/updates/now-ga-mongodb-atlas-is-available-as-a-microsoft-azure-native-integration/ · keywords: Azure Native MongoDB ANM
- [statement] Native provisioning creates a new Atlas organization and links its billing to an Azure Marketplace plan; MongoDB directs customers connecting an existing organization to its separate Marketplace Pay-as-you-go listing. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/partner-integrations/azure.md · keywords: Azure Native MongoDB ANM · also: https://www.mongodb.com/resources/products/integrations/atlas-azure-native-integration
- [statement] MongoDB documents granting the initiating user Atlas Organization Owner and recommends configuring Microsoft Entra ID SSO after organization creation. Its quick-start resource also lists SSO configuration as a setup step. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/partner-integrations/azure.md · keywords: Azure Native MongoDB ANM · also: https://www.mongodb.com/resources/products/integrations/atlas-azure-native-integration
- [statement] Removing the Azure integration resource does not delete the Atlas organization: Microsoft requires separate deletion in Atlas, while MongoDB says unlinking preserves the organization. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-05-26) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/partner-integrations/azure.md · keywords: Azure Native MongoDB ANM · also: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/partner-solutions/mongo-db/faq
- [statement] Irurueta's third-party technical guide describes the Marketplace integration as a procurement and billing wrapper around the vendor control plane; the guide explicitly discloses AI assistance and cites vendor documentation, so it does not independently validate operational behavior. (low confidence) — https://www.irurueta.com/cloud/azure/redis-and-partner-databases.html · keywords: Azure Native MongoDB ANM
